judgments.question: When a break is triggered during a turn, what happens to excess movement, the triggering reward, the remaining turn and next turn?

requested_parts.part: Ignore Break movement beyond the final space
requested_parts.observed_quote: When the Break token reaches its last space, ignore any movement beyond it, and the player who moved it there gains 1 X-token. Finish the triggering player's current turn; the break then occurs. After the break, play continues clockwise with the next player. The break token is reset to the starting space for the player count.
requested_parts.summary_support_quote: **The Break track.** At the start of the game and after each break, the Break token sits on the starting space for your player count. requested_parts.part: Build II adds Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary

requested_parts.summary_support_quote: - **Side II:** Build **as many different buildings as you like** with a **maximum total size equal to the strength** — but never 2 identical buildings in the same Build action. When you build the Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary you may immediately — and only once per building — move **all suitable animals that fit** from standard enclosures into it, choosing separately for each. Unique buildings can never be built with this action — they only come into play via their Sponsor cards.

judgments.question: Give the four Association task strengths, side-I/II task limits, worker requirements when repeating a task before a break, and whether other players workers matter.

requested_parts.part: Task strengths are reputation two, partner three, university four and conservation five
requested_parts.observed_quote: The four Association tasks are reputation (strength 2), partner zoo (3), university (4), and conservation-project work (5). Association I performs exactly one task; Association II performs one or more different tasks whose total task value is at most action strength. Each task needs an active worker. If one of your workers is already on the chosen task, place 2 workers to repeat it; if 3 of yours are there, you cannot use it again until after a break. Other players' workers do not affect your ability to perform a task.
requested_parts.summary_support_quote:
- **Increase reputation (strength 2):** increase your zoo's reputation by **2**, taking any track bonuses you reach.
  - **Gain partner zoo (strength 3):** take a partner zoo from the Association board onto the lowest empty partner-zoo space of your map (take any printed bonus immediately). All your partner zoos must be from different continents, maximum 4 total; the third (or fourth) requires the upgraded Association action. If every zoo currently on the board is one you already have, or you cannot place it, you cannot perform this task. Each partner zoo reduces the cost of Animal cards from its continent by 3 money per continent icon, provides 1 icon of that continent (usable for card effects and conservation projects), and some Animal cards require one.
  - **Gain university (strength 4):** take a university from the Association board onto the lowest available university space and take its covered-space bonus immediately. **Also gain the reputation printed on the university tile immediately.** You cannot take a duplicate university. Universities grant reputation and research icons and are the only way to increase your hand limit to 5.
  - **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). **The Base Conservation Projects below the board never move and are never replenished**, even when fully supported.

judgments.question: How may a Conservation Project enter play, what are support conditions/once limits, where does its token come from, when is the uncovered bonus taken, and what happens to overflowing projects/tokens?

requested_parts.part: A new project must be played and supported immediately
requested_parts.observed_quote: Conservation-project work can support a project already in play or play one from hand and support it immediately; Association II can instead play the new project from the reputation-range display, paying its folder number, with no refill until turn end. New cards enter the leftmost space above the Association board and push others right. To support, meet an unoccupied condition and place one of your zoo-map support tokens on it; a project can normally be supported by you only once, and each reward level holds one token total across all players. Take the token from the left edge of your map, activating its bonus immediately (before or after the project reward, your choice; recurring bonuses also pay each break). If a project is pushed beyond the player-count limit, discard the rightmost project and return its support tokens to their owners' supplies, not their map; the activated bonuses stay active.
requested_parts.summary_support_quote: - **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). **The Base Conservation Projects below the board never move and are never replenished**, even when fully supported.
requested_parts.explanation: This requested proposition is resolved in the quoted answer, with frozen-summary support.

requested_parts.summary_support_quote: - **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). The **total value** of the tasks may not exceed your action's strength (it may be less). Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. When doing conservation project work you may also play the new Conservation Project card directly **from the display** (within reputation range, paying the folder number as an additional cost; no replenish until turn end). In addition you may make exactly **1 donation**: pay the smallest amount of money still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain **1 conservation point**. The printed donation costs are **2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10**, then the repeatable **12-money** space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each subsequent donation costs **12 money** (no further tokens placed). A donation requires having performed at least 1 association task in the same action, needs no worker, and is limited to 1 per Association action.

judgments.question: For release projects, must printed standard enclosure size match exactly; what appeal/icons/reputation/conservation are lost or retained, and how do you free enclosure space?

requested_parts.part: Use printed standard-size bands: two-minus accepts one/two, three accepts three, four-plus accepts four/five
requested_parts.observed_quote: Match the animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement to the depicted size category: 2− accepts size 1 or 2, 3 accepts size 3, and 4+ accepts size 4 or 5; exact matching is not required within 2− or 4+. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, then discard it and its icons. Keep its conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects. If it could live in a special enclosure and its indicated tokens can be removed, you must remove those tokens; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, or if none, the smallest meeting size alone; if none meets size, flip none. This also applies to flock animals.
requested_parts.summary_support_quote: - **Release into the wild** projects work differently: instead of counting icons, discard 1 Animal card with the specific icon from your zoo; match the animal’s **printed standard-enclosure requirement to the depicted size category**: **2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5**. You cannot use an animal from another category. The actual enclosure tile occupied, or capacity in a special enclosure, does not define this category. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, **before** gaining conservation points; discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its indicated number of special-enclosure tokens can be removed, you **must remove those tokens**; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, else the smallest meeting size alone, else none if no occupied enclosure meets size. This applies even to flock animals. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not.
requested_parts.explanation: This requested proposition is resolved in the quoted answer, with frozen-summary support.

judgments.question: State conservation milestone rewards at 2,5,8,10; exact end trigger timing including gains on another player turn; last turns; Final Scoring cap; victory-point formula and tiebreak.

requested_parts.part: At two conservation choose an upgrade or an additional active worker
requested_parts.observed_quote: At 2 conservation, choose an Action-card upgrade or activate another worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or the Bonus token by that space (if available); the money option remains. The first player reaching 10 makes all players discard one Final Scoring card; if no one reaches 10, all discard one before final scoring. Check game end at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal earned during another player's turn waits for your turn end or a break to trigger it. If triggered at a player's turn end, that player finishes and all others take one more turn; if triggered during a break, everyone takes one more turn. Each Final Scoring card can grant at most 4 conservation. VP equals Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter; highest positive score wins, ties go to the player with most project supports, then tied players share victory.
requested_parts.summary_support_quote: - **2 conservation points:** either upgrade one of your Action cards (flip it) or activate an additional association worker (take a lying worker from the lowest space below the notepad onto the notepad). Each player who reaches space 2 gets this choice.

At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or the Bonus token by that space (if available); the money option remains. The first player reaching 10 makes all players discard one Final Scoring card; if no one reaches 10, all discard one before final scoring. Check game end at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal earned during another player's turn waits for your turn end or a break to trigger it. If triggered at a player's turn end, that player finishes and all others take one more turn; if triggered during a break, everyone takes one more turn. Each Final Scoring card can grant at most 4 conservation. VP equals Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter; highest positive score wins, ties go to the player with most project supports, then tied players share victory.

judgments.question: When you earn an Action card upgrade, what happens to its position, when is the new action usable, when does it count for conditions, and can all five cards be upgraded?

requested_parts.part: Flip one chosen side-I Action card to side II
requested_parts.observed_quote: Flip one Action card of your choice from I to II; it remains in its current slot. Its improved action is usable from your next action, but it counts as upgraded for conditions immediately. An upgrade during an action does not change that action's strength or capabilities. One upgrade reward allows an alternative choice, so you cannot upgrade all five cards.
requested_parts.summary_support_quote: **Upgrading Action cards.** All Action cards start on side I. When you receive a card upgrade, flip one Action card of your choice from side I to side II (it stays in its slot); its improved action is available **from your next action**, while it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. The current action keeps the strength and kind set at its start; an upgrade gained during it does not add side-II capabilities to it. There are **4 ways to upgrade** an Action card: on the Conservation track, on the Reputation track, and when you gain your second partner zoo or your second partner university. One of them allows you to choose an alternative — so you cannot upgrade all of your Action cards.
requested_parts.explanation: This requested proposition is resolved in the quoted answer, with frozen-summary support.

requested_parts.part: Donation requires Association II
requested_parts.observed_quote: Association II may make exactly 1 donation if you have performed at least 1 Association task in the same action; no worker is needed for the donation. Pay the smallest amount still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain 1 conservation point. Printed costs are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then a repeatable 12-money space; skip setup-blocked spaces. After every space but the last is covered, each further donation costs 12 and places no additional token. The per-action limit remains one donation.

Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. judgments.question: Which displayed symbols count as icons in your zoo, which do not, do effects count their own card and repeated icons, and which text wins if a card conflicts with a general rule?

requested_parts.part: Upper-right Animal and Sponsor icons count
requested_parts.observed_quote: Zoo icons are the upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, partner-zoo and university icons, and upper-left water/rock requirements. Left-side conditions and Conservation Project icons do not count as zoo icons. An effect referring to an icon on its own card counts that icon; doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. Card text takes priority over general rules.
requested_parts.summary_support_quote: Card text takes priority over general rules. Cards count their own icons for instant effects and recurring triggers. Only upper-right card icons, partner-zoo/university icons and upper-left water/rock requirements count as zoo icons; left-side conditions and conservation-project icons do not. Doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes: touching one water hex in a larger water area gives one adjacency; several edges touching that hex still give only one. Water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

judgments.question: Where are Constriction 1/2 tokens placed, can they stack, how do they change strength and multiplied actions, and when are they removed?

requested_parts.part: Constriction one goes on slot five and two on slots four and five
requested_parts.observed_quote: Constriction 1 places a token on the affected player's highest-slot card (slot 5); Constriction 2 places tokens on slots 4 and 5. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. Each affected action loses 2 strength, including each execution of a multiplied action, though X-tokens can restore strength. Return tokens after the card is used or without effect at the break.
requested_parts.summary_support_quote: - **Constriction:** affect all other zoos ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. An affected action loses two strength; this applies to each execution of a multiplied action. X-tokens can restore strength. At effective strength zero or below, use enough X-tokens to reach at least one, use the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. Return the token after acting, or without effect in the break.

judgments.question: Where is an earned Multiplier placed, how are two actions resolved, how do X-tokens and after-finishing effects work, may a break stop the second action, and when is the token returned?

requested_parts.part: Immediately place gained Multiplier on its named card
requested_parts.observed_quote: Place a gained Multiplier immediately on its named Action card; a bonus-tile Multiplier may go on any card. On its next use, execute the action twice in succession at the same base strength, moving the card only after both executions; each X-token boosts only one execution. Defer 'after finishing' effects until both are done. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the entire turn is finished. Return used Multiplier tokens to supply; unused ones are removed at the next break.
requested_parts.summary_support_quote: **Multiplier.** Place a gained token immediately onto the named Action card; a bonus-tile Multiplier may go on any card, including Animals. On its next use you may execute that action twice in succession at the same base strength, moving its Action card only after both executions. Each X-token boosts only one execution. Each additional Multiplier used adds one execution: two tokens permit up to three actions, not four. You may choose different permitted options within each regular execution (Sponsors could play cards then take money). A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but may not mix one X-token action with one regular action. Defer after-finishing effects until all executions are done. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the entire turn is finished. Return used tokens to the supply; an unused token is removed during the next break.

judgments.question: Where are Venom tokens placed, can they stack, what happens when a marked card is used, what happens at turn end if no token was removed, and when do unused tokens expire?

requested_parts.part: Place Venom on lowest-slot cards starting with one

Using a marked card removes its Venom token and avoids all Venom fees that turn, including by using the X-token alternative if you hold fewer than 5 X-tokens. This includes the alternative X-token action if you hold fewer than five X-tokens. Otherwise, if any Venom remains on your cards at turn end, pay two money. If you cannot, undo the turn and choose a different action; you cannot escape the fee by spending all your money. The next break clears unused tokens without effect.
